docs.title: Blog Management Application
docs.text:
Welcome to the Functional Specification Documentation for the Blog Management Application.

This documentation provides a comprehensive overview of the system’s purpose, scope, user roles, and core functionalities. It serves as a guide to understand how the application operates from both Admin and User perspectives — outlining the features, behavior, and business logic behind the platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Blog Management Application is a web-based platform that allows administrators to create, publish, and manage blog content while enabling users to read, comment, and subscribe for updates. It combines content control, user interaction, and newsletter communication into a single streamlined system.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The goal of this documentation is to define the functional specifications of the Blog Management Application — describing what the system should do, how it should behave, and how users interact with it. It does not cover technical implementation details such as architecture, code, or deployment.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Content Management: Admins can create, edit, and publish blogs.
  • User Engagement: Readers can explore blogs, post comments, and subscribe for updates.
  • Moderation: Admins can approve or reject comments to maintain quality discussions.
  • Communication: The newsletter system keeps readers informed about new blog posts.
  • Dashboard Insights: The admin dashboard provides an overview of blogs, comments, and subscribers.

docs.title: Roles and Access
docs.text: Role Description Admin Manages all blogs, comments, and newsletter operations. User Reads blogs, posts comments, and subscribes to newsletters.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The Blog Management Application bridges the gap between creators and readers through a structured, efficient, and user-friendly platform. It ensures easy content management for administrators and an engaging, interactive experience for users.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: The Blog Management Application allows content creators to publish and manage blogs while readers can interact through comments and newsletter subscriptions. It’s an alternative to complex CMS tools, focused on simplicity, engagement, and control.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Simplify blog publishing
  • Enable user engagement via comments
  • Build reader retention through newsletters
  • Provide a single admin dashboard for control and insights

docs.title: 2.1 Purpose
docs.text: The purpose of this project is to design and develop a Blog Management Application that enables administrators to create and manage blog content while allowing users to read, comment, and subscribe for updates. The system aims to deliver a lightweight, user-friendly alternative to heavy CMS platforms, focusing on simplicity, engagement, and control.

docs.title: 2.2 Scope
docs.text:
A. User-Facing Features - View published blogs with category-based filtering. - View blog details, author information, and publish date. - Add comments on blogs (pending admin approval). - Subscribe to the newsletter using an email address.

B. Admin-Facing Features - Secure login and authentication system for administrators. - Create, edit, publish, unpublish, and delete blogs. - Moderate user comments (approve/reject). - Manage newsletter subscribers. - Send newsletters to subscribers directly from the dashboard. - Access dashboard analytics showing blog count, drafts, comments, and subscribers.

docs.title: 2.3 Objectives
docs.text:
The key objectives of this project are as follows:

Objective Description Success Indicator Simplify Blog Management Provide a clean admin dashboard for creating and managing blogs. Admin can publish or edit blogs with ease. Enhance Reader Engagement Enable users to comment and interact with blog content. Increase in approved comments and engagement metrics. Ensure Content Quality Implement moderation for all comments before publishing. zero unapproved or spam comments visible publicly. Centralized Control Allow the admin to manage content, comments, and newsletters in one place. Single dashboard managing all core operations.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text: Role Description Usage Frequency Admin Manages blogs, comments, and newsletters. Frequent User (Reader) Reads blogs, comments, and subscribes. Frequent Subscriber Receives newsletters and updates. Occasional

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Admin: Publish and maintain blog content.
  • User: Read blogs, add comments, and subscribe.
  • Subscriber: Receive newsletters about new posts.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
• Users will have stable internet access.
  • Subscribers provide valid email addresses.
  • Admin users are verified and registered.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Only approved comments will be displayed publicly.
  • Newsletter frequency will be regulated to prevent spam.
  • Email delivery relies on external email service availability.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• MongoDB (Database Storage): Used to store all blog content, user comments, newsletter subscribers, and admin credentials securely.

  • NodeMailer (Email Delivery): Required for sending newsletters and notifications to subscribed users.

  • Cloud Hosting Environment: Ensures uptime and public accessibility for both the frontend and backend services.

docs.title: FRD-001: Blog Management
docs.text:
• Description: Admin can create, edit, publish, or delete blogs.
  • Priority: Must-have
  • Actor: Admin
  • Use Case: "As an Admin, I want to publish new content for readers."

docs.title: FRD-002: Comment Management
docs.text:
• Description: Users can post comments; Admins can approve or reject them.
  • Priority: Must-have
  • Actors: User, Admin

docs.title: FRD-003: Newsletter Subscription
docs.text:
• Description: Users can subscribe via email to receive updates.
  • Priority: Should-have

docs.title: FRD-004: Admin Dashboard
docs.text:
• Description: Admin can view total blogs, comments, and subscribers.
  • Priority: Must-have

docs.title: FRD-005: Authentication and Authorization
docs.text:
• Description: Secure admin login with restricted access.
  • Priority: Must-have

docs.title: 6. Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text: Category Requirement Security Only authenticated admins access dashboard. Usability Responsive, intuitive user interface. Scalability Must handle future growth in content. Compatibility Support for Chrome, Firefox, Edge.

docs.title: Key Data Entities
docs.text: Entity Description Blog Contains blog details, category, and author. Comment Stores comments linked to a specific blog. Subscriber Stores email addresses for newsletters. User Represents admin and users.

docs.title: Data Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Create: Admin adds blogs, users comment, subscribers join.
  • Modify: Admin updates blogs.
  • Delete: Admin removes blogs or comments.
  • Archive: Comments remain in the database for record-keeping.

docs.title: Key Screens
docs.text:
• Home Page: Displays blogs and newsletter form.
  • Blog Details Page: Shows content, author, and comments.
  • Admin Dashboard: Provides analytics and management tools.
  • Add Blog Page: Used by admin to create or update content.
  • Newsletter Page: Manage and send newsletters.

docs.title: 10. External Interfaces
docs.text: Interface Description Email Service Used for sending newsletters. Web Browser Primary interface for users and admins. Hosting Environment Web server hosting for accessibility.

docs.title: 11. Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition Admin Authorized user managing content. User Site visitor who reads and comments. Subscriber User who receives newsletters. Dashboard Admin interface showing system metrics. Comment Feedback posted by a reader on a blog.

docs.title: Data Flow Diagram
docs.text:
This diagram illustrates how data moves through the Blog Management Application — from the end user's browser to the backend and database.

graph TD
    U[User] -->|Uses| FE[Frontend React App]
    FE -->|API Calls| API[Backend Express API]
    API -->|Read/Write| DB[(Database - MongoDB)]
    API -->|Authenticate| AUTH[Auth Service]
    API -->|Send| MAIL[Email Service]

    DB -->|Return Data| API
    AUTH -->|Verify| API

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
• User interacts with the React frontend
  • Frontend sends API requests to the backend
  • Backend communicates with:
  • Database → for storing blogs, comments, users
  • Auth Service → for authentication & authorization
  • Mail Service → for notifications and newsletters
